scenario:
A biotechnology company is developing an enterprise-level Bioinformatics Platform to manage and analyze genomic sequence data. The platform is designed to support research teams in genomic annotation, variant analysis, and comparative genomics. It should facilitate the integration of genomic data from various sources and provide tools for in-depth sequence analysis, including mapping, alignment, and feature annotation.

The system must handle large datasets of genomic sequences, each characterized by contigs, start and end positions, genes, gaps, coverage metrics, identity scores, accession numbers, and product descriptions. Researchers require the ability to annotate sequences with functional information, track sequence variations, and visualize genomic features.

The platform will support collaborative research projects, offering advanced user management with roles and permissions tailored to bioinformaticians, geneticists, and data analysts. It will provide comprehensive reporting capabilities and support for integrating external databases and data-sharing with the scientific community. The platform should also implement robust data versioning and provenance tracking to ensure the reproducibility and integrity of genomic analyses.
